exercises.name: Back Squat
cues: Bar on the shelf of your shoulders, not your neck; squeeze the shoulder blades.
Big breath in and brace before you unrack, not after.
Sit down between your hips, knees tracking over your toes.
Drive the whole foot into the floor on the way up.

exercises.name: Front Squat
cues: Elbows high, bar resting on your shoulders -- the fingers only guide it.
When the elbows drop the bar follows, so keep them up all the way.
Stay upright and sit straight down between the hips.
Expect noticeably less than your back squat.

exercises.name: Safety Bar Squat
cues: The padded yoke sits on your shoulders; hold the handles in front of you.
It tips you forward more than a straight bar -- fight to stay upright.
Useful on days your shoulders will not let you hold a normal bar.

exercises.name: Snatch-Grip Deadlift
cues: Grip the bar wide, at the rings, so the hips start lower.
Chest up and shoulders pulled back before the bar moves.
Expect a lot less weight than a normal deadlift -- that is the point.

exercises.name: Weighted Chin-Up
cues: Palms toward you, hands about shoulder width.
Start from a dead hang and pull the collarbones to the bar.
Lower under control -- do not drop out of the top.

exercises.name: Weighted Dip
cues: Lean the torso forward slightly and let the elbows travel back.
Stop when the upper arms reach parallel -- deeper is not better here.
Keep the shoulders down and away from the ears throughout.

exercises.name: Belt Squat
cues: The load hangs from the hips, so the spine carries nothing.
Stand tall and squat between the handles without pulling on them.
Useful on a day when the back is the part that is tired.

exercises.name: Deadlift
cues: Bar over mid-foot, shins almost touching it before you take your grip.
Chest up, lats tight, and pull the slack out of the bar before you pull.
Push the floor away rather than yanking the bar up.
Finish standing tall -- do not lean back at the top.

exercises.name: Trap Bar Deadlift
cues: Stand in the middle of the bar with the handles level at your sides.
More like a squat than a straight-bar pull -- the knees bend more.
Chest up, push the floor away, stand tall to finish.
Expect a little more than your straight-bar deadlift.

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift
cues: Wide stance, toes turned out, hands gripping inside your knees.
Open the hips and push the knees out as you set up.
The bar stays against your legs the whole way up.
Hips and shoulders rise together -- do not let the hips shoot up first.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
cues: Start standing, then push the hips back with only a soft bend in the knee.
The bar stays in contact with your thighs the whole way down.
Stop when the hamstrings run out, not when the bar reaches the floor.
Much lighter than a deadlift -- this is a hamstring lift, not a pull.

exercises.name: Rack Pull (Above Knee)
cues: Set the pins so the bar starts just above your kneecaps.
Higher pins mean a shorter pull -- the load is not comparable to a floor deadlift.
Shoulders back and lats tight before you break it off the pins.
Lower it back to the pins under control; do not bounce it.

exercises.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
cues: Shoulder blades on the bench, feet flat, shins vertical at the top.
Pad the bar across your hips -- it will dig in otherwise.
Squeeze the glutes to finish and keep your ribs down.
Chin tucked: look forward, not up at the ceiling.

exercises.name: Squat Clean
cues: Pull as for a power clean, then keep dropping into a full front squat.
Meet the bar early -- do not wait and catch it low and slow.
Stand up out of the bottom before thinking about the next rep.

exercises.name: Depth Push-Up
cues: Start with a hand on each of two low boxes and drop to the floor between them.
Catch the fall and drive back up onto the boxes in one motion.
Stay rigid -- the hips must not sag as you land.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Bench Throw
cues: Use the Smith rails so the bar leaves the hands safely at the top.
Light load, maximal intent -- throw it, do not press it.
Catch with soft elbows and reset before the next rep.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Push Press
cues: Short dip from the knees, then drive the bells straight overhead.
The dip is vertical -- the chest must not tip forward.
Lock the elbows before the feet settle.

exercises.name: Landmine Push Press
cues: Hold the bar end at the shoulder, dip, and drive it along the arc.
The path is forward and up, not straight up -- follow the bar.
Keep the ribs down; do not lean back to finish the rep.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Jerk
cues: From the rack, dip and drive, then dip a second time under the bells.
The arms do not press -- the legs send it and you drop beneath.
Stand up out of the catch with the bells stacked over the shoulders.

exercises.name: Curtsy Lunge
cues: Step one foot back and across behind the other, like a curtsy.
Keep the hips square to the front -- do not let them open up.
Drive back up through the front heel, not the back toe.

exercises.name: Zercher Carry
cues: Carry the bar in the crooks of the elbows with the hands clasped.
Ribs down and elbows up -- the bar is trying to fold you forward.
Short steps, hard brace, shallow breaths.

exercises.name: Landmine Rainbow
cues: Hold the bar end at chest height, both hands, arms nearly straight.
Sweep it hip to hip in an arc and let the trunk turn with it.
Move the bar with the trunk -- do not throw it with the arms.

exercises.name: Russian Twist
cues: Sit with the heels down or hovering, chest tall and back straight.
Rotate the ball from hip to hip, turning the ribs, not just the arms.
Stop if the low back rounds; that is the end of the set.

exercises.name: Depth Jump
cues: Step off a knee-high box -- do not jump off it or use a taller one.
Leave the ground again as fast as you can after landing.
Ground time is the target; height is only the result.

exercises.name: Hurdle Hop
cues: Bounce over each hurdle with the feet together and the knees cycling up.
Stay stiff through the ankles and spend as little time down as you can.
End the set when the heels start touching the floor.

exercises.name: Tuck Jump
cues: Jump and pull the knees to the chest, not the chest to the knees.
Land soft on the balls of the feet and go straight into the next one.
Stop when the knees stop reaching the same height.

exercises.name: Lateral Bound
cues: Push sideways off one leg and land on the other.
Stick the landing -- no hop or stumble once the foot is down.
Cover distance across the floor, not height off it.

exercises.name: Split Jump
cues: Start in a lunge, jump up and switch the legs in the air.
Land in the same lunge depth you took off from.
The front knee tracks over the foot on every landing.

exercises.name: Tall-Kneeling Med Ball Throw
cues: Kneel tall with the hips locked out -- no sitting back on the heels.
Throw with the trunk and arms only; the legs cannot help you here.
Keep the ribs down instead of arching the back for more range.

exercises.name: Acceleration Sprint
cues: Start low and rise gradually -- no popping upright in the first steps.
Push the ground back behind you rather than reaching forward.
Full effort the whole way; walk back to recover between reps.

exercises.name: Build-Up Run
cues: Start at a jog and add speed smoothly across the whole distance.
Reach about 90% by the end, then float -- never strain.
Shoulders and jaw stay loose the entire way.

exercises.name: Flying Run
cues: Use a 20 m run-in to reach speed before the marked zone.
Hold the speed through the zone; do not accelerate inside it.
Tall posture, relaxed hands, quick ground contacts.

exercises.name: Hill Sprint
cues: Lean into the hill from the ankles, not from the waist.
Short, punchy steps -- drive the knees, do not over-stride.
Walk all the way down; the descent is the rest.

exercises.name: Sled Push
cues: Arms locked out, body in one line from heel to head.
Short powerful steps, fully extending the back leg each time.
Keep the hips low -- rising up kills the drive.

exercises.name: Band-Resisted Sprint
cues: Set the band so it slows you slightly, never so it stalls you.
Hold the forward lean the band creates and push back hard.
End the rep when your form breaks, not when the band stops you.

exercises.name: A-Skip
cues: Skip with a knee drive to hip height, opposite arm forward.
The foot strikes down and back, directly under the hip.
One small hop per leg -- rhythm matters more than height.

exercises.name: B-Skip
cues: An A-Skip, then extend the lower leg forward at the top.
Claw the foot back down under the hip, never landing in front.
Hips stay tall; the reach happens below the knee only.

exercises.name: High Knees
cues: Knees to hip height, torso tall, no leaning back.
Quick ground contacts -- think frequency, not height.
Arms drive from the shoulder, hands to chin and hip.

exercises.name: Straight-Leg Bound
cues: Legs stay nearly straight; the motion comes from the hips.
Pull the ground back with the whole leg, landing on the ball of the foot.
Stay tall -- no forward bend at the waist.

exercises.name: Wall Acceleration Drill
cues: Hands on the wall, body in one line at about 45 degrees.
Drive one knee up, then punch the foot down under the hip.
The support heel stays off the ground for the whole set.

exercises.name: Ankling
cues: Stay tall and cycle the foot under the hip, never out in front.
Tiny steps -- the heel barely leaves the ground.
Land on the ball of the foot and snap it straight back up.

exercises.name: A-March
cues: Drive one knee to hip height with the opposite arm forward.
No flight phase -- one foot stays on the ground throughout.
Punch the foot straight down under the hip, not ahead of it.

exercises.name: Carioca
cues: Travel sideways, swinging the trail leg in front then behind.
Let the hips rotate freely while the shoulders stay square.
Quick feet -- the rhythm matters more than the ground covered.

exercises.name: Backpedal
cues: Sit into a low hip position and reach back with each step.
Stay on the balls of the feet -- the heels never touch down.
Keep the chest over the knees so you do not fall backward.

exercises.name: Lateral Shuffle
cues: Half-squat stance, feet pushing apart and never crossing.
Drive the ground away with the trail leg on every step.
Keep the head level -- no bobbing up and down.

exercises.name: Fast-Leg Drill
cues: March three steps, then snap one leg through at full speed.
The fast leg cycles heel to hip, knee up, foot down.
Use the same leg for the whole rep; switch on the next one.

exercises.name: Falling Start
cues: Stand tall and lean from the ankles until you must catch yourself.
Let gravity start the run -- do not step until you have to.
Keep the first few steps low, pushing back instead of reaching.

exercises.name: Three-Point Start
cues: Front foot two shoe-lengths back, opposite hand down on the line.
Hips a little above the shoulders, weight forward onto the hand.
Rip the down arm back as the front leg drives you out.

exercises.name: Power Skip
cues: Skip for height rather than distance -- drive the knee up and hold.
The opposite arm punches to eye level as the knee rises.
Land under the hips and go straight back up.

exercises.name: Ruck March
cues: Pack the load high and tight against the upper back, straps snug.
Walk tall with a quick, short stride; do not lean forward from the waist.
Build distance before load; a ruck punishes the feet long before the legs.

exercises.name: Sled March
cues: Load it so you can walk continuously, not so you have to fight it.
Stay tall behind the sled, arms long, and drive through the legs.
Steady pace for time; if it turns into a grind, take weight off.

exercises.name: Backward Walk
cues: Walk backward over flat, clear ground, reaching back with the toe first.
Roll from toe to heel and keep the knee soft as the foot lands.
Glance over a shoulder now and then; never do this on uneven ground.

exercises.name: Trail Run
cues: Shorten the stride and pick the feet up more than you would on road.
Look three or four steps ahead, not down at your feet.
Keep the effort easy; let the terrain, not the pace, provide the work.

exercises.name: Front Plank
cues: Elbows under the shoulders, feet hip width, body in one line.
Squeeze the glutes and tuck the ribs down so the hips do not sag.
Brace hard and keep breathing; do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Side Plank
cues: Elbow under the shoulder, feet stacked or staggered.
Push the hip up until shoulder, hip and ankle make one line.
Keep the top shoulder back; do not let the chest roll toward the floor.

exercises.name: Copenhagen Plank
cues: Side plank with the top leg's inner thigh resting on a bench.
Lift the hips and the bottom leg until the body is one line.
Start with the bottom knee bent; straighten it only when that is easy.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
cues: Lie on your back and press the low back flat into the floor.
Lift the shoulders and legs just clear, arms reaching overhead.
If the low back lifts, raise the legs higher until it flattens again.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
cues: On your back, arms up and knees over the hips, low back flat.
Lower one arm and the opposite leg, keeping the back flat.
Move slowly and exhale as you reach; return, then alternate.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
cues: On all fours, hands under the shoulders and knees under the hips.
Reach one arm and the opposite leg out long, level with the back.
Keep the hips square; a glass of water on the low back should not spill.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
cues: Stand side-on to the cable or band with both hands at the chest.
Press straight out and resist the pull trying to rotate you.
Stand tall and square; the work is in not turning.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
cues: Kneel with the wheel under the shoulders and the back flat.
Roll out only as far as the low back stays flat, then pull back.
Keep the ribs tucked; an arching back means you went too far.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
cues: Hang from the bar with the shoulders pulled down, not slack.
Raise the legs by curling the pelvis up, not just the hips.
Lower under control; no swinging between reps.

exercises.name: Toes to Bar
cues: Hang tall, shoulders active, and start from a small hollow.
Curl the pelvis and drive the toes up to touch the bar.
Control the way down; kip for rhythm, never for the whole rep.

exercises.name: Reverse Crunch
cues: Lie on your back, knees bent, hands flat beside the hips.
Curl the pelvis up so the hips leave the floor.
It is a short move; lifting the knees alone does nothing.

exercises.name: Cable Crunch
cues: Kneel facing the stack, hands holding the rope beside the head.
Crunch by rounding the spine toward the knees with the hips still.
The hips must not hinge; if they do, lighten the load.

exercises.name: L-Sit
cues: Hands on the floor or parallettes, shoulders pressed down.
Lift the hips clear and hold the legs straight out in front.
Tucked knees are the scaled version; keep the chest tall either way.

exercises.name: Bear Crawl
cues: On hands and toes with the knees hovering just off the floor.
Move the opposite hand and foot together, in small steps.
Keep the hips low and level; do not let them sway side to side.

exercises.name: Suitcase Hold
cues: Hold one heavy weight at your side with the shoulders level.
Stand tall and resist the lean toward the loaded side.
Grip hard and keep the ribs down for the whole hold.

exercises.name: Bicycle Crunch
cues: On your back, low back flat, hands resting light behind the head.
Bring one elbow toward the opposite knee by turning the ribs.
Do not pull on the neck; slow rotation beats fast pedalling.

exercises.name: Supine Windshield Wiper
cues: Lie on your back, arms out wide, knees bent over the hips.
Lower the knees toward one side while both shoulders stay down.
Go only as far as the shoulders stay flat, then return through the middle.

exercises.name: Side Plank Reach-Through
cues: Set a side plank, elbow under the shoulder, top arm to the ceiling.
Reach the top hand under the body, turning the ribs, then open back up.
Keep the hips high throughout; the rotation comes from the trunk.

exercises.name: 90/90 Hip Switch
cues: Sit with both knees bent 90 degrees, front shin and back shin on the floor.
Rotate the knees over to the other side, keeping the chest tall.
Move under control; the hips do the work, not a swing of the torso.

exercises.name: Couch Stretch
cues: Back foot up the wall, front foot flat and forward of the knee.
Square the hips and tuck the tailbone under before leaning up.
Breathe out and hold; never force it past a strong stretch.

exercises.name: World's Greatest Stretch
cues: Step into a deep lunge, back leg long, front foot flat.
Drop the same-side elbow toward the instep, then rotate that arm to the ceiling.
Follow the hand with the eyes; one slow rep per side, never a bounce.

exercises.name: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
cues: Half-kneeling, front foot flat, back knee under the hip.
Tuck the tailbone under first, then shift forward an inch.
The stretch belongs at the front of the back hip, not the low back.

exercises.name: Thoracic Extension over Foam Roller
cues: Roller across the mid-back, hands behind the head, hips down.
Extend over it a few inches at a time, pausing where it is stiff.
Keep the ribs from flaring, and never roll the lower back.

exercises.name: Cat-Cow
cues: On all fours, hands under the shoulders and knees under the hips.
Round the spine one segment at a time, then reverse into extension.
Move with the breath and stop short of any pinch in the low back.

exercises.name: Thread the Needle
cues: From all fours, slide one arm under the body, palm facing up.
Let that shoulder rest down while the hips stay stacked over the knees.
Return by reaching the same arm to the ceiling, then alternate.

exercises.name: Banded Shoulder Dislocate
cues: Hold a light band wide, arms straight, thumbs up.
Sweep the band overhead and behind you, keeping the elbows locked.
Widen the grip until it passes without shrugging or arching the back.

exercises.name: Scapular Wall Slide
cues: Stand with the back, arms and hands flat against the wall.
Slide the arms overhead without letting the ribs or wrists leave the wall.
Stop where contact breaks; that range is the rep.

exercises.name: Shoulder CARs
cues: Stand tall, one arm straight, and trace the largest circle you can.
Keep the ribs down and the opposite shoulder still.
Slow and deliberate; a single circle should take several seconds.

exercises.name: Hip CARs
cues: Stand tall, hold something for balance, lift one knee to hip height.
Trace the biggest circle you can with that knee, out and around.
Keep the pelvis square; only the hip moves.

exercises.name: Ankle Dorsiflexion Rock
cues: Half-kneeling, front foot flat, heel glued to the floor.
Drive the knee forward over the toes, then rock back out.
The moment the heel lifts you have gone past the range.

exercises.name: Adductor Rock-Back
cues: On all fours, extend one leg out to the side with the foot flat.
Rock the hips back toward the heels, then return.
Keep the low back flat; the stretch belongs in the inner thigh.

exercises.name: Deep Squat Hold
cues: Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out, sink as low as you can.
Elbows inside the knees, pushing them gently out.
Chest up and heels down; hold a doorframe if you need balance.

exercises.name: Child's Pose
cues: Kneel, big toes together, knees wide, sit back onto the heels.
Reach the arms long and let the chest sink toward the floor.
Breathe into the back of the ribs and let the shoulders relax.

exercises.name: Dead Hang
cues: Hang from a bar, hands shoulder-width, grip firm.
Let the shoulders travel up toward the ears and stay relaxed.
Keep the ribs down, and step off before the grip fails.

exercises.name: Leg Swing
cues: Hold a wall for balance and stand tall.
Swing one leg front to back, then side to side, staying relaxed.
Let the range build over reps rather than forcing the first swing.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Stretch
cues: Hands on a wall, one foot back, back leg straight.
Press the back heel into the floor and lean in from the ankle.
Keep the back foot pointing forward, not turned out.

exercises.name: Seated Hamstring Stretch
cues: Sit tall, one leg straight, the other foot tucked to the inner thigh.
Hinge forward from the hips rather than rounding the back.
Stop at a strong stretch behind the thigh, breathe out, and hold.

exercises.name: Standing Quad Stretch
cues: Stand tall, steady yourself on a wall, pull one heel to the glute.
Keep the knees side by side and the tailbone tucked under.
Ease the hip forward; do not arch the lower back to get more.

exercises.name: Supine Figure-Four Stretch
cues: Lie on your back, one ankle crossed over the opposite thigh.
Reach through and draw the bottom thigh toward your chest.
Keep the head and shoulders down; it should bite deep in the glute.

exercises.name: Seated Spinal Twist
cues: Sit tall, one knee crossed over the opposite leg, that foot flat.
Rotate toward the top knee, the elbow acting as a gentle lever.
Turn from the mid-back and keep both sit bones on the floor.

exercises.name: Prone Press-Up
cues: Lie face down, hands under the shoulders, hips staying on the floor.
Press the chest up only as far as stays comfortable.
Let the lower back relax into it, and back off if anything pinches.

exercises.name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
cues: Bring one arm straight across the chest at shoulder height.
Draw it in with the other forearm, just above the elbow.
Keep the shoulder down rather than shrugged toward the ear.

exercises.name: Overhead Triceps Stretch
cues: Reach one hand down your spine, elbow pointing at the ceiling.
Use the other hand to draw that elbow gently back and in.
Keep the ribs down instead of arching the lower back.

exercises.name: Soleus Stretch
cues: Set up like a calf stretch, then bend the back knee toward the wall.
Keep that heel flat on the floor the whole time.
It should sit low near the Achilles, not up in the calf belly.

exercises.name: Kneeling Ankle Stretch
cues: Kneel with the toes tucked under and sit back onto the heels.
Share the weight evenly, and come up if the toes cramp.
Hands on the floor in front take weight off if it is too strong.

exercises.name: Wall Lat Stretch
cues: Hands on a wall at hip height, feet walked back, arms straight.
Sink the chest toward the floor with the hips over the heels.
Feel it along the side of the ribs and under the armpits.

exercises.name: Butterfly Stretch
cues: Sit with the soles of the feet together and the heels drawn in.
Sit tall first, then hinge forward from the hips.
Let the knees fall open on their own; never push them down.

exercises.name: Upper Trap Stretch
cues: Sit tall, one hand under the opposite thigh to anchor that shoulder.
Tilt the ear toward the other shoulder until it is a mild stretch.
No rotation and no hard pulling; the neck takes a gentle dose only.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
cues: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and close to the hips.
Push through the heels until hips, knees and shoulders line up.
Squeeze the glutes at the top; do not arch the low back to get higher.

exercises.name: Knee CARs
cues: Seated or standing on one leg, hold the thigh still with both hands.
Trace the largest slow circle you can with the heel.
Only the knee moves; if the hip joins in, shrink the circle.

exercises.name: Ankle CARs
cues: Seated, lift one foot clear of the floor and hold the shin still.
Trace the biggest circle you can with the toes, both directions.
Keep the knee quiet; the movement is all ankle.

exercises.name: Squat to Stand
cues: Feet shoulder width, reach down and hold on under the toes.
Pull yourself into a deep squat and lift the chest tall.
Keep the grip and straighten the legs to stand; repeat smoothly.

exercises.name: Walking Quad Pull
cues: Walking forward, catch one ankle behind you and pull the heel to the hip.
Stand tall and squeeze the glute on that side.
Hold for a step, release into the next stride, then alternate.

exercises.name: Inchworm
cues: From standing, hinge over and walk the hands out to a straight plank.
Keep the hips level and the ribs down as you walk out.
Walk the feet back to the hands, legs as long as is comfortable.

exercises.name: Scorpion
cues: Lie face down with the arms out wide and the palms flat.
Reach one heel across and behind toward the opposite hand.
Keep both shoulders down; rotate only as far as they stay on the floor.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Hip Hinge
cues: Feet hip width, hands on the belly and low back to feel the position.
Push the hips back and let the chest fall, keeping the back flat.
Go only as low as the back stays flat, then drive the hips forward.
